findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now an abstract class and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but implements none of its abstract members (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the newly added `build_occurrence_and_event_data`). Because StatefulDetectorHandler uses abc.ABC/abc.abstractmethod, this class remains abstract, so `Detector.detector_handler`'s `group_type.detector_handler(self)` will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler` for any Detector whose type is `metric_alert_fire`. Previously the class was instantiable and simply returned an empty list. Implement the required methods (even if stubs), or don't wire this abstract class as the group type's detector handler. The adjacent comment `# TODO: This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction` is also now stale.

findings.title: test_dedupe builds the expected occurrence with the wrong group key and will fail
findings.body: In `TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe`, the expected occurrence is built with `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH)`, but the call under test is `handler.evaluate_group_key_value("group_key", ...)` (the expected result's group_key is "group_key"). The mock helper derives the occurrence fingerprint from the supplied group key, so the expected occurrence gets fingerprint `[f"{id}:val1"]` while the actual occurrence produced by `evaluate_group_key_value` gets `[f"{id}:group_key"]`. Since `IssueOccurrence`/`DetectorEvaluationResult` equality compares the fingerprint (and in any case the objects differ), the assertion `handler.evaluate_group_key_value(...) == expected_result` will not pass. The expected occurrence must be built with "group_key".

findings.title: evaluate docstring still documents a list return value
findings.body: `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` was changed to return `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, but its docstring still says it 'returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`' and that there is 'one result for each group key result'. This is misleading for implementers of the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data` hook and for callers; update the docstring to describe the returned dict.

findings.title: New hook's value argument is never asserted by the tests
findings.body: `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` accepts `value` but never uses it, so none of the tests verify that the correct group value is passed into the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data` hook. This is visible in `test_state_results_multi_group`, which builds the expected occurrence for `group_2` with value `6` even though the packet value for `group_2` is `10`, and in `TestEvaluate.test_dedupe`, which passes `6` while the evaluated value is `8`. A regression where `evaluate_group_key_value` passed the wrong value would go undetected; the mock should incorporate `value` into the occurrence or event data.
